item.name: AI safety
item.description: Operation of AI systems that does not endanger human life, health, property, or the environment; improved through responsible design, deployment practices, simulation and in-domain testing, monitoring, and human intervention.
item.grounding_span:
Other practical approaches for AI safety often relate to rigorous simulation and in-domain
testing, real-time monitoring, and the ability to shut down, modify, or have human inter-
vention into systems that deviate from intended or expected functionality.

item.name: safety risks
item.description: Risks of AI systems leading to injury, death, or other endangerment; prioritized by context and severity.
item.grounding_span:
Different types of safety risks may require tailored AI risk management approaches based
on context and the severity of potential risks presented.

item.name: AI risk management
item.description: Tailored approaches to managing AI risk, whose urgency and thoroughness scale with the severity of potential harm and which should align with sector-specific guidance.
item.grounding_span:
Different types of safety risks may require tailored AI risk management approaches based
on context and the severity of potential risks presented.

item.name: resilience
item.description: Ability of an AI system and its ecosystem to withstand unexpected adverse events or changes, maintain function and structure, degrade safely, and return to normal function.
item.grounding_span: Security and resilience are related but distinct characteristics.

item.name: security
item.description: Maintenance of confidentiality, integrity, and availability through protection mechanisms preventing unauthorized access and use; encompasses resilience plus protocols to avoid, protect against, respond to, and recover from attacks.
item.grounding_span:
While resilience is the abil-
ity to return to normal function after an unexpected adverse event, security includes re-
silience but also encompasses protocols to avoid, protect against, respond to, or recover
from attacks.

item.name: transparency
item.description: Extent to which information about an AI system and its outputs is available to individuals interacting with it, tailored to lifecycle stage and to the role or knowledge of AI actors.
item.grounding_span:
Meaningful transparency provides access to appropriate levels
of information based on the stage of the AI lifecycle and tailored to the role or knowledge
of AI actors or individuals interacting with or using the AI system.

item.name: accountability
item.description: Answerability for the outcomes of AI systems; presupposes transparency and varies across cultural, legal, sectoral, and societal contexts.
item.grounding_span:

AI systems.

item.name: explainability
item.description: Representation of the mechanisms underlying an AI system's operation; answers how a decision was made.
item.grounding_span:
Risk from lack of explainability may be managed by describing how AI systems function,
with descriptions tailored to individual differences such as the user’s role, knowledge, and
skill level.
